https://www.worcesternews.co.uk/news/265.text: West Mercia Police Crime Worcester Wylds Lane murder probe - dead man was 'quiet with a cat' By James Connell Chief Reporter Share 0 Comments 3 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share 0 Comments This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. HORRIFIED neighbours have spoken of their shock after the death of a 'quiet man with a cat' as police launch a murder probe. Neighbours of the 42-year-old Damian Buczek who died following an incident in Wylds Lane in Worcester, have spoken of their shock at his death, some calling it a 'tragedy'. However, few of the neighbours in the terraced houses in Wylds Lane or nearby Dent Close knew much about Mr Buczek or had spoken to him, knowing him only by sight. As previously reported, a 46-year-old man has been arrested in connection with Mr Buczek's death and remains in custody. Mr Buczek was described by neighbours as a 'quiet man with a cat' who would smoke outside the terraced property, but none knew details of his personal life or how long he had been in Worcester. His Facebook profile says he is self-employed and from Tarnobrzeg, a city in south-eastern Poland. Members of the Polish community, including chair Tom Wisniewski, have paid their own tributes to Mr Buczek, saying they have been left heartbroken and shocked by his death. Councillors, including Cllr Jabba Riaz and Cllr Adam Scott, are among those to express their shock at the violent nature of Mr Buczek's death, and extend their condolences to his family and friends. INVESTIGATION: Police outside home in Wylds Lane as they launch a murder probe (Image: Newsquest) One neighbour reported seeing lots of comings and goings at the address after midnight at the address in Wylds Lane in the past, including taxis pulling up outside and people going to the address, which is now sealed off with police tape. However, the neighbour had heard nothing on the night of the incident itself because he was at work at the time. Two of his next-door neighbours believed he had a cat called Fiona which they had told him he needed to look after, and they would sometimes see him smoking in front of the house. READ MORE: Man arrested on suspicion of the murder of Damian Buczek "I've never talked to him. He's very quiet," she said of Damian Buczek, recognising his face when she saw a news report on the murder. She added: "We are really shocked about this. He was our neighbour, and we can't believe it. He's died." PRESENCE: West Mercia Police remained at the scene in Wylds Lane in Worcester on Friday (Image: James Connell/Newsquest) Another close neighbour, who again declined to be named, said: "It's very hard. It's happened. That's life. I didn't know him." One neighbour, Leonard Hensher, 78, of Dent Close, said the only thing he knew of the incident was when multiple police cars arrived at the scene. READ MORE: Wyld's Lane: Murder investigation after death of man in Worcester "I didn't think they had so many police cars. I think most of the people living over there are Polish, but there is one Englishman. I'm not really shocked or surprised," he said, pointing out some arrows he said had been shot over a roof in the direction of his house. He added: "We do get some police coming up and down here from time to time." A police cordon remains around a terraced house near the junction with Dent Close as officers continue their investigation. Police were called to an address in Wylds Lane shortly after 9pm on Tuesday, September 1, following reports that a man had been found with life-threatening injuries. Mr Buczek was taken to hospital, where he later died despite the efforts of medical staff. A 46-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder on Thursday evening, September 3, in connection with his death. He remains in police custody while enquiries continue. READ MORE: Community in shock following Wyld's Lane murder investigation Cllr Adam Scott, a councillor for Cathedral ward, said: "We don't know any details of this tragic incident, but we know the whole of the City will be dismayed at any violent incident which happens in our community. Crime rates are falling both nationally and locally. We want to emphasise that Worcester is a safe and friendly place to live. We hope the police investigation proceeds apace. Our sympathies go to the relatives of the deceased. " Detective Chief Inspector Gareth Lougher, from the Major Investigations Unit, said: “Our investigation continues to move at pace, and tonight we have arrested a 46-year-old man in connection with Damian’s death.” Officers are particularly asking for information about Damian’s movements between Monday, August 31, and Tuesday, September 1. Detective Chief Inspector Lougher said: “In particular, we would like to hear from anyone who saw Damian between Monday 31 August and Tuesday 1 September.” Police also want footage from people who were in the Wylds Lane area during that period. https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/andrew-tate-ad.text: Andrew Tate is accused of possessing 'extreme pornography' allegedly depicting sexual intercourse with a horse and an eel, according to extradition documents submitted by British authorities.The allegations form part of a wider criminal case against Tate, 39, and his brother Tristan, 38. The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) has decided to prosecute Andrew Tate on additional charges involving indecent images of a child and extreme pornography, as well as further counts of rape, arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, and assault occasioning actual bodily harm. The brothers deny the allegations and have not yet appeared before a British court in relation to the charges.Disturbing Material Allegedly Found on DeviceThe extradition papers allege that British investigators found footage involving a horse and an eel on a device attributed to Andrew Tate. The specific descriptions of the alleged material come from the documents and are not findings of fact.The CPS said Andrew Tate faces 19 additional charges relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography. The alleged offences date from July 2010 to August 2017.The CPS stressed that its decision to prosecute is not a finding of guilt or criminal conduct. It said its role is to independently assess whether charges should be presented for a court to consider, and warned that the proceedings are active and the defendants are entitled to a fair trial.Documents Detail Separate Child Image AllegationsThe extradition papers also describe an allegation involving a sexualised video in which Tate and an adult woman are alleged to appear alongside a female child. Another allegation, according to the extradition documents, concerns a WhatsApp group chat involving Andrew Tate and three other people. The documents allege that Tate sent images of a child and stated that she worked on a webcam.The documents allege that Tate wrote, 'One guy said he would pay her $1,000 every day if she could f*** herself. So I told her she had to do it.' Tate then allegedly sent a video involving the child, accompanied by the message, 'And finally she learnt how.' He is also alleged to have shared a screenshot showing a $1,000 payment into a bank account before stating, 'This man sends me $1,000 every day.'Prosecutors Allege 'Lover Boy' SchemeThe newly published documents also provide a fuller account of the wider British prosecution case. British law enforcement alleges that the Tate brothers used a 'lover boy' model to lure women with promises of romantic relationships before coercing them into producing online pornography.According to a Bedfordshire Police detective's summary cited by Reuters, women were allegedly encouraged to travel to Romania after being told they could pursue relationships and earn money through Andrew Tate's webcam business. Once there, the detective's summary alleges, the women became financially dependent on the brothers, who often confiscated their passports.'The prosecution case is that Andrew Tate and Tristan Tate used and threatened physical and sexual violence in order to maintain control and compliance,' the detective wrote, according to Reuters.Tate Brothers Challenge ExtraditionThe case has put renewed focus on Tate, a former professional kickboxer who gained wider public attention after appearing on the UK reality show Big Brother in 2016. He later built a large online following by promoting views on masculinity, relationships, wealth, and success, with clips of his speeches and interviews widely circulated on social media.His online presence grew into a prominent social media profile, while his comments about women drew widespread scrutiny. His rise as an influencer preceded the criminal investigations and legal proceedings that later involved him and his brother in the UK and Romania.The brothers were arrested in Miami on 18 July after Britain sought their extradition from the US. They are dual US and British citizens and remain in custody in Miami as they contest the extradition proceedings. A final hearing date has not yet been set.Their lawyer, Joseph McBride, has challenged the extradition case, arguing that the identities of the alleged victims have not been disclosed to the defence. McBride said the accusations could not be 'meaningfully tested' and argued, 'No American court should be asked to surrender a person to a foreign country on the word of secret accusers.'The brothers also face separate legal proceedings in Romania, where they have been under investigation over alleged offences since 2022. Both deny wrongdoing.
